sentences.text: 11. The 'misbranded food' as defined in Section 3(zf) of the FSS Act includes an article of food offered or promoted for sale with false, misleading or deceptive claims either upon the label of the package or through advertisement.

12. Section 23 of the Act specifically provides that no person shall manufacture, distribute, sell or expose for sale or despatch or deliver to any agent or broker for the purpose of sale, any packaged food products which are not marked and labelled in the manner as may be specified by regulations.
13. Regulation 2.2 of the FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011, relates to the labelling of the food article.

14. Regulation 2.2.8 of the FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011, specifically provided that the batch number or code number or lot number, which is a mark of identification by which the food can be traced in the manufacture and identified in the distribution, shall be given on the label.
15. Regulation 2.2.9 of the FSS (P&L) Regulations, 2011, specifically provides that the date, month and year in which the commodity is manufactured, packed or prepacked, shall be given on the label.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to mention here that the appellants have not disputed that requisite information have not been given on the Principal Display Panel.
On the other hand, it has been printed on the bottom of the tin container.
The scheme of the Act as framed by the Legislature and the subsequent judicial pronouncement have made it clear that the provisions of this legislation have to be construed strictly.

18. I consider that the Ld. Chief PP for the State has rightly submitted that if the words of the statute are precise and unambiguous, then there is no room for the interpretation of these words in any other manner.
The courts are duty bound to give strict interpretation of such legislature and to give effect to it.
The purpose of the Food Safety & Standard Act is to protect the interest of the consumers and to ensure that general consumers who goes to buy the food articles have all the requisite information.
If a layman goes to purchase an article and particularly, of a famous and established manufacturer, he has explicit faith that he or she will get the proper material.
The purpose of giving of such information on the Principal Display Panel is to ensure that the innocent consumer is not prejudiced in any manner.
FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 14 of 16 19.

20. I consider that provisions of the present Act are to be strictly interpreted and if these information are to be given on the Principal Display Panel, they should have been given on the Principal Display Panel.

I consider that benefit of due diligence as provided under Section 80 of the Act also cannot be extended to the present appellants as the FBO or the supplier or the distributor are duty bound to ensure that the goods which they are selling further are not misbranded and comply with all the provisions of the Act and Regulations.
22. I have gone through the impugned order dated 16.12.2019 of the Adjudicating Officer and do not find any illegality or impropriety in the said order.
The Adjudicating Officer has passed a very detailed and reasonable order.
All the contentions of the appellants have thoroughly been discussed and there is no ground to interfere in the order of Ld. ADM.
Hence, the order of the Adjudicating Officer is upheld.

However, in FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 15 of 16 view of the facts and circumstances of the case, I consider that a lenient view may be taken against the appellants.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The FSO filed a complaint before the Ld.ADM, New Delhi under 3.1.1(3) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011("FSS Rules" in short) against the appellants for the adjudication of the offences under Sections 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zf)(A)(i)(a), 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) and 3(1)(zf)(C)(iii) of FSS Act along with violation of Regulation No.2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 and 2.3.2 of FSS (P&L) Regulations.
Milk Producers Union Ltd. and the remaining respondents had purchased it through valid bill and they are entitled to benefit of guarantee under Section 26(4) of the Act as sample commodity was taken into the same condition as was FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs.
The respondents/appellants herein had also claimed the benefit of due diligence under Section 80 of FSS Act.
The Adjudicating Officer after taking into account the averments of the respondents/appellants herein reached to the conclusion that respondents have violated the provisions of the FSS Act as well the Regulations contained in the FSS (P&L) Regulations and imposed the penalty under Section 52 of the FSS Act.
The plea of the appellant is that there is no violation of Section 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) of FSS Act.
The impugned order was also assailed on the ground that the FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No.
03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 7 of 16 Food Analyst was neither the recognised nor any opportunity was granted as per Section 43 of the FSS Act.
The appellants also took a plea that the respondents/appellants herein were entitled to the benefit of guarantee and due diligence under Section 26 and 80(B)(2) of the FSS Act, 2006.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The appellants have submitted that Regulation 2.3.2 of FSS FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No.
02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 8 of 16 (P&L)
Regulation also empowers to give all these information on "another place" and therefore, it is not mandatory to give all these information on the Principal Display Panel.
The appellants have relied upon Hindustan Lever Ltd. Ors. Vs. Food Inspector 2007(1) 299 and R. Chandramohan Vs. FSO 2019(1) FAC 547 Madras.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO
FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 13 of 16 17.
The courts are duty bound to give strict interpretation of such legislature and to give effect to it.
The purpose of the Food Safety & Standard Act is to protect the interest of the consumers and to ensure that general consumers who goes to buy the food articles have all the requisite information.
If a layman goes to purchase an article and particularly, of a famous and established manufacturer, he has explicit faith that he or she will get the proper material.
The purpose of giving of such information on the Principal Display Panel is to ensure that the innocent consumer is not prejudiced in any manner.
opennyai_summary.decision:
22. I have gone through the impugned order dated 16.12.2019 of the Adjudicating Officer and do not find any illegality or impropriety in the said order.
The Adjudicating Officer has passed a very detailed and reasonable order.
Hence, the order of the Adjudicating Officer is upheld.
However, in FSAT No. 01/20 Suresh Chand Ors. Vs. FSO, FSAT No. 02/20 Vikas Guleria Anr Vs. FSO & FSAT No. 03/20 D.T. Patel Anr Vs. FSO Page No. 15 of 16 view of the facts and circumstances of the case, I consider that a lenient view may be taken against the appellants.
Hence, I impose a penalty of Rs.10,000/ each on appellant Suresh Chand and Sh. Aman Gupta &
Sh. Amit Gupta, both partners of M/s Durga Agencies.
A consolidated penalty of Rs.25,000/ is also imposed upon appellants Vikash Guleria and M/s Gujarat Coop Milk Marketing Federation Ltd.
Further, a consolidated penalty of Rs.25,000/ is also imposed upon appellants D.T. Patel and M/s Banaskantha District Coop Milk Producers Union Ltd.
However, the manufacturing company shall take all corrective action to rectify the mistake and shall ensure that henceforth all particulars are printed on the Principal Display Panel only as provided in Regulation 2.3.2 of the Food Saftey and Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulations, 2011.
23.
All the aforesaid appeals are accordingly, dismissed.
Copy of the order be sent to the Ld. ADM.
24.
